headline: The worst week for the S&P 500 since April 2025: chips and AI power fell hardest after the vote, Friday's bounce came on half Thursday's volume, oil lost 13%, and next week brings CPI on Tuesday and China's rare earth deadline.
summary: The dashboard is still on Nov 5 closes (prices_as_of 2026-11-05) and the refresh did not fill Nov 6 from Massive (closes_from_massive is empty), so every Nov 6 close here is from Massive and the dashboard is a day behind. For the week SPY fell 2.70% to 735.29 and QQQ 4.98% to 656.10, 13.6% under its Oct 6 record; the S&P 500 index lost 2.7%, its worst week since April 2025 (Massive, The Closing Print). The chip ETF SMH fell 11.20% and energy (XLE) 12.00%, while banks (XLF) rose 1.15% and gold (GLD) 4.71% (Massive). Friday was a partial bounce: QQQ rose 1.40% on 70.7 million shares, about half of Thursday's 130.7 million, so buyers were thin. Brent settled at $98.32, about 13% lower on the week, as Iran sent a proposal through Qatar while tanker attacks went on (Gulf News, FinanceFeeds). The scorecard, now graded by her rule, shows 4 finished swings, 3 wins, an average of +0.12R, and the PMCC trial had no passing day in 10 trading days. Next week: Rocket Lab Monday, CPI and China's rare earth deadline Tuesday, Veterans Day Wednesday (bond market closed), Cisco and Applied Materials Thursday.

regime.why: The Nasdaq 100 is in a correction, the selling moved from AI suppliers to chips to the big AI buyers, and Friday's bounce came on half the volume of Thursday's drop. Strong jobs and wages keep a December Fed hike in play, so there is no rate cut cushion. The VIX fell to 25.64 Friday but rose 32% for the week.

signals.title: Week in review: the vote hit the AI build, then the whole market; Friday's bounce was thin
signals.since_yesterday: Friday's bounce: QQQ +1.40% on about half of Thursday's volume, and chips won back only about a third of Thursday's drop.
signals.what_happened: Week of Nov 2 to 6, Massive closes Oct 30 to Nov 6: SPY -2.70% (735.29), QQQ -4.98% (656.10), DIA -0.95%, IWM -2.03%, SMH -11.20%, SOXX -13.13%, XLE -12.00%, XLF +1.15%, XLP +0.74%, XLV -0.04%, GLD +4.71%, TLT +0.10%. Biggest drops on the AI map: Lumentum -35.94% (538.59), Marvell -28.11% (141.20), SanDisk -27.44%, Astera Labs -26.28%, Micron -22.01%, Vertiv -21.35%, Bloom -14.73%, CoreWeave -15.44%. Winners: AppLovin +71.21%, Airbnb +15.57%, Delta +8.80%, Amazon +7.88%, Becton Dickinson +7.07%. The story ran in four steps: Monday Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum in stock; Tuesday Democrats won both chambers; Wednesday the AI suppliers fell on data center limits while the big AI buyers rose; Thursday everything fell (SPY -4.41%, QQQ -6.49%, SMH -11.21%) after top Democrats called for a national data center moratorium (CNBC). Friday QQQ rose 1.40% on 70.7 million shares against 130.7 million Thursday; Nvidia rose 2.78% on 180 million shares against 306 million (Massive). StockTitan's tally of eight chip stocks shows they won back 36% of Thursday's drop by the close, after about 40% early. Jobs beat (165,000) and University of Michigan sentiment came in at 51.0 against 47.5 expected (CNBC via StockTitan). At 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, the deal is worth 635.40 on Friday, so LITE trades 15.2% below it (my math).
signals.so_what: A bounce on half the volume of the drop is short covering and bargain hunting, not funds coming back. The tell for a real turn is a strong up day on heavier volume than Thursday. Second order: the market is now pricing politics into the AI build (permits, power prices, state limits), and that hits the suppliers with the most debt and the least pricing power first. Third order: if chip prices stay down, stock and debt funding for AI builders gets dearer, which can slow orders in 2027 even if demand holds. What would make this wrong: a clear signal that a national pause will not pass a split government, and the next big chip reports (Nvidia Nov 17 on the Yahoo calendar) showing orders still rising.
signals.for_you: Swing: no new longs while QQQ sits under its 10% correction line (about 683.69) and up days come on light volume. Puts: none in chips or AI power; a 17% day (AMD, Micron on Nov 5) can repeat. Long term: wait for the chart; NVDA (186.64) and AMD (449.04) are still under their buy zones on the dashboard.

signals.title: Scorecard: how the calls did
signals.what_happened: The scorecard was graded Nov 7 on Nov 5 data, now by her swing rule (a trigger is a close over the entry on at least 1.5 times the 50 day volume, the fill is that close, a win is a close at the target, R is from the fill). Swings: 21 calls, 4 finished, 3 wins (ABBV +0.25R, LNG +0.36R, BDX +0.86R), 1 loss (EOG -1.0R), average +0.12R; 8 never triggered (two of them, XOM and GILD, confirmed only after they were already past the target); 3 open (PFE -0.32R, WST -0.47R, AMGN -0.36R); 6 still waiting (EWT, COP, PSX, ANET, ZBRA, TMO). Cash secured puts: 15 logged, none finished; the first expiry is Nov 20. Long term buys: 120 calls; 52 of 115 beat SPY after 5 days (45%, average 2.6 points behind) and 27 of 55 after 20 days (49%, average 0.54 points behind). Brief signals: 191 calls; 83 of 148 right after 5 days (56%, average 0.33 points ahead) and 22 of 46 after 20 days (48%, average 0.16 behind). The new chart check for lower highs and lower lows (added Oct 31) fails for 5 of the 29 names priced in or near a buy zone on Nov 5 closes: HII, BEN, AXP, JPM and DASH. It is the only failed check for JPM, so by itself it moved one name out of 'Buy zone now' (and took the JPM put idea off the list after Oct 31); the other four also fail another check.
signals.so_what: These are tiny samples: 4 finished swings and no finished puts prove nothing. What works: the volume rule kept the dashboard out of setups that then fell. ZBRA (322.02 against a 387.01 entry), ANET (170.80 against 215.33) and NVDA (186.64 against 240.59) never confirmed (Massive, Nov 6), and under the old intraday grading ZBRA and ANET had counted as three losses. Brief signals are slightly ahead of SPY at 5 days. What does not work: the fills come late. Across the 7 fills, the confirming close sat on average about 63% of the way from the entry to the target (my math), so wins are small (+0.25R to +0.86R) while a stop still costs a full 1R. Long term buys trail SPY at 5 days and are about even at 20 days, too early to judge. A data fix this week: COP closed under its 135.75 stop on Nov 5 before it ever triggered, but the scorecard still listed it as waiting; the code now voids a setup that closes under its stop first (with a test), so COP moves to never triggered on the next refresh.
signals.for_you: One rule change to consider: a chase limit. Skip a trigger when the confirming close is more than 5% above the entry, and wait for a pullback toward the pivot instead. Three of the 7 fills broke that line (LNG +6.4%, AMGN +6.8%, WST +8.7% above entry); so far that group is one small win (+0.36R) and two open trades under water. That is too few to prove anything, so the honest step is to track it beside the main rule for a month before adopting it. Until then, read the swing average as 'no edge shown yet', not as a loss.

signals.title: PMCC trial, two week review: no day passed in 10 trading days
signals.what_happened: The poor man's covered call rules started on Oct 24. In the 10 trading days from Oct 26 to Nov 6, no name passed on any day, so the trial log has no examples. The reasons repeated: the 'Buy zone now' names were either in falling groups (chips, fintech, energy), had earnings inside a 30 to 45 day short call (NICE, LIVN, RELY, CF, AFRM, ADI), or had options too thin to trust (GD, LDOS, AEP, COF traded 0 to 4 contracts on the dates checked in the Nov 6 put screen). The closest call was GD on Nov 6: in its zone with no report until late January, but its options barely trade. On Nov 5 closes the dashboard's 'Buy zone now' list is PFE, ZS, LDOS, AEP, LMT and RELY.
signals.so_what: No examples in two weeks means there is nothing yet to build a Setups screen on. It also fits the market: a PMCC's long call loses about twice the stock's percentage drop, so in a correction with the VIX near 26 the leverage works against her. The names calm enough to pass the chart rules tend to have the thinnest option markets, which is exactly where a deep in the money long call is hardest to buy at a fair price.
signals.for_you: Verdict: change the trial, do not build the screen yet. Keep the rules, but check PMCC once a week in the Saturday brief instead of every day, and only on names with an active option market (a liquid long dated call). Review again on Dec 5. If there are still no passing examples by then, drop it. Most weeks the right answer is no PMCC.

signals.title: Oil: Brent lost about 13% this week; tanker attacks go on while Iran answers through Qatar
signals.since_yesterday: Brent settled at $98.32 Friday, almost flat, ending the week about 13% lower; a crew member died on a tanker near Hormuz.
signals.what_happened: Brent's January contract settled at $98.32 on Nov 6, up 3 cents, and WTI at $90.83, up 31 cents (Gulf News, FinanceFeeds). From the $113.43 January settle on Oct 30, Brent fell about 13.3% (my math). FinanceFeeds says more than 16%, which matches the expired December contract's $117.64; the same contract comparison is the fairer one. Iran sent a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar, Qatar proposed steps to narrow the gap, and no deal to reopen Hormuz has been announced (Reuters via FinanceFeeds, Gulf News). Flows through the strait are below 60% of capacity, and a crew member died in an explosion on the tanker MT Velos Sapphire; the cause is not established (FinanceFeeds, Gulf News). Energy stocks fell harder than oil: XOM -11.42%, CVX -9.73%, COP -11.53%, EOG -11.12% for the week (Massive). OPEC's monthly report is due Nov 11; OPEC+ meets Nov 29.
signals.so_what: The market is pricing a deal before one exists. If talks stall, the war premium comes back fast; if a deal is signed, oil can fall further, which helps inflation and airlines and hurts producers. Who gets paid either way: tanker owners and insurers while attacks continue. Energy stocks now trade with the broad market, so they can fall on a day oil rises.
signals.for_you: Swing: no oil setups; the four oil plans closed by the stop rule on Nov 4. Puts: none in energy. Long term: no energy name has a buy verdict. Watch DAL: cheaper fuel helped it rise 8.80% this week (87.20, Massive).

signals.title: Quantum and space reports beat: IonQ grew 336%, AST SpaceMobile signed for Firefly engines
signals.what_happened: IonQ reported Q3 revenue of $173.8 million, up 336%, raised its 2026 revenue guide to $505 million to $515 million from $450 million to $460 million, and said remaining performance obligations more than doubled to $1.2 billion (SEC 8-K). Part of the growth comes from the SkyWater purchase. IONQ rose 23.42% Friday to 32.62 (Massive). AST SpaceMobile said it will build its own reusable rocket, Blacklift, with Firefly's Miranda and Vira engines: $250 million for engines for the first three launches, $250 million over three years for engineering support, and a license to make the engines, with launches from late 2028 (SEC 8-K). StockTitan reported the deal as worth more than $1.3 billion; the filing lists about $500 million, so we use the filing. FLY rose 36.80% to 20.76 and Karman 42.13% to 45.61 after a record quarter (Massive, StockTitan).
signals.so_what: In a week when investors sold anything tied to AI spending, small space and quantum names rose on contracts and revenue. That is the money trail at work: government and carrier money is still flowing to these chokepoints. Second order: AST building its own rocket is a vote against relying only on SpaceX for launch, which helps Firefly and suppliers like Karman. What would make this wrong: these are thinly profitable or loss making companies, and one day jumps of 20% to 40% often fade.
signals.for_you: No action. IONQ, FLY and KRMN have no buy verdict, and RKLB (53.07) is rated Avoid on the dashboard and reports Monday. No chasing a 40% day.

signals.so_what: Kinder buying after an 11.5% weekly drop says an insider who built the business sees the gas pipeline story intact: data centers still need gas power even if permits slow, and pipelines get paid on volume, not on AI stock prices. signals.title: Week ahead, Nov 9 to 13: CPI Tuesday, China's rare earth deadline, Veterans Day, Cisco and Applied Materials
signals.what_happened: Monday Nov 9: Rocket Lab reports after the close (Yahoo, TipRanks); AST SpaceMobile also reports (Yahoo calendar). Tuesday Nov 10: October CPI at 8:30am ET (5:30am Pacific), per several calendars and FinanceFeeds; Continuum Economics expects headline +0.2% for the month and about 3.9% from a year ago (3.5% in September) and core +0.2% and about 2.8%; TD Securities sees headline +0.30% and core +0.21%. Also Tuesday: China's suspension of its October 2025 rare earth export rules ends, with no extension notice found as of Nov 7 (Rare Earth Directory, Startup Fortune); AEP goes ex dividend; Firefly reports. Nov 10 to 11: US brokered Russia Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi (Latin Times, Whalesbook). Wednesday Nov 11: Veterans Day; stocks trade, the bond market is closed on SIFMA's recommendation; OPEC monthly report; Corteva reports. Thursday Nov 12: Cisco, Applied Materials and Cerebras after the close (StockTitan, Yahoo); Nebius is listed Nov 10 by one calendar and Nov 12 by Yahoo. Saturday Nov 14: FDA decision date for Summit's ivonescimab in EGFR mutated lung cancer (SEC 8-K). Starship Flight 15: the FAA planning date was no earlier than Nov 8, but SpaceX has not announced a date (Space Launch Schedule). Correction: our Nov 4 brief listed possible US and Iran talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10 to 11 from one report; the confirmed Abu Dhabi talks on those dates are about Russia and Ukraine, and we found no US and Iran meeting there.
signals.so_what: CPI is the week's big test: after a strong jobs report, a hot inflation number would make a December hike likely and hit the long duration tech stocks again. With bonds closed Wednesday, Treasury yields can gap on Thursday's open after two days of news. A rare earth lapse would bring back Chinese licenses on more items, which helps US magnet and mining names but squeezes defense and auto supply chains. Cisco and Applied Materials are the first test of AI demand after the chip crash.
signals.for_you: Swing: no new entries before Tuesday 8:30am ET. Puts: no new puts before CPI; the weekday screen resumes Monday. AEP is in its buy zone and goes ex dividend Nov 10, so a short call across that date carries early assignment risk. Long term: none of the 'Buy zone now' names (PFE, ZS, LDOS, AEP, LMT, RELY) reports this week on the Yahoo calendar. MP (35.41, Avoid) is the name to watch on the rare earth date.

cycle.quadrant_why: Hiring is strong (165,000 jobs in October, unemployment 4.1%, wages up 3.1%; BLS), while consumers feel poor (Michigan sentiment 51.0; CNBC via StockTitan). September CPI was 3.5% and Continuum expects October near 3.9% on Tuesday. Oil fell about 13% this week, which helps November's inflation but not October's.
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening, late. The Fed's range is 3.75% to 4.00%; before Friday's jobs report Reuters put December hike odds above 65%, and the strong report pushed them higher (CME FedWatch via StockTitan). The 10 year ended at 4.86%, down 8 basis points for the week as money hid in bonds and gold.
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. Public debt is high, and the AI build now leans on stock and bond markets that just repriced chips by 11% in a week. Higher funding costs for builders are the channel to watch.
cycle.big_cycle: Internal order: a split government after the vote, with data center politics moving into state houses and Congress. External order: tanker attacks near Hormuz while Iran negotiates through Qatar; Russia and Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi; China's rare earth pause ends Tuesday. Technology: AI results are still strong, but prices are being set by fear of rules.
tailwinds: Jobs and wages are strong; this is not a recession selloff.
Oil fell about 13%, easing future inflation and fuel costs.
Defense, space and quantum contracts keep flowing (IonQ, AST SpaceMobile, Kratos buying by ARK).
headwinds: CPI on Tuesday could seal a December hike.
Friday's bounce came on half of Thursday's volume.
A rare earth lapse could squeeze defense and auto supply chains.

history.when: 2022: the Fed hiking cycle and the tech bear market
history.what: The Nasdaq Composite lost 33.1% in 2022 and the S&P 500 19.4%, the worst year since 2008, as the Fed raised rates seven times; sharp rallies along the way did not hold (AP via CBS News).
history.lesson: In a hiking cycle, the fastest bounces in tech often fail. Wait for a strong up day on rising volume before calling a bottom.

history.when: March 2000 to October 2002: the telecom build bust
history.what: The Nasdaq Composite fell about 78% from its March 10, 2000 peak as the network build ran ahead of profits, and the suppliers fell hardest.
history.lesson: When investors doubt the buyers will keep spending, suppliers to the build fall first and furthest, even while they still report growth.

cycle.differences: Unlike 2022, the Fed is near the end of its hikes, not the start, and unemployment is low. Unlike 2000, today's biggest AI buyers pay mostly from cash flow and the threat is permits and politics, not a lack of customers. The risk that does rhyme: crowded positions in suppliers, sold together.
cycle.for_you: Swing: stand aside until a strong day on rising volume. Puts: no new puts before CPI; cash is a position. Long term: the calm 'Buy zone now' names (LDOS, AEP, LMT) held up; PFE and ZS slipped under their zones Friday, so wait for the dashboard to recheck them.

principle.text: Pain plus reflection equals progress (paraphrase of Principles).
principle.applied: The scorecard shows late fills shrink the wins. Instead of trusting the rule or dropping it, track the 5% chase limit beside it for a month and let the numbers decide.

actions.options: The weekday put screen (9g) does not run on weekends; it resumes Monday. research/put_ideas.json stays empty, and no put is suggested in this brief. Before CPI on Tuesday, no new puts. AEP goes ex dividend Nov 10: any short call across that date carries early assignment risk. PMCC: none. Two week review: no passing day in the 10 trading days since Oct 24. Recommendation: keep the rules, check them once a week on Saturdays only on names with an active long dated option market, and decide on Dec 5 whether to drop the trial. Never quote a premium from this brief; check the chain and the live bid.
